AML Guardian / Browser automation

19 scenarios. One command.

Each scenario opens a real browser and works through the investigation workspace like a person would. It loads four synthetic test cases first and checks what you should see at every step. Watch at your own pace with captions and a Pause button, or run them all in the background.

Open the application ↗ Beginner's guide

How to run

From the project folder in Terminal:

./scenarios.sh                                # menu: pick scenarios, watch or not, speed
./scenarios.sh list                           # list every scenario
./scenarios.sh run all                        # run everything in the background (about 1–2 minutes)
./scenarios.sh run sanctions-hold --watch     # watch one scenario with captions
./scenarios.sh run stories --watch --speed slow
./scenarios.sh run ai-draft-verifier --model  # use the local AI if Playwright starts the API
OptionWhat it does
--watchShows the browser with a caption bar describing each step. Click Pause or Resume at any time.
--speed slow|normal|fastHow long each caption stays on screen while watching. The default is normal.
--modelIf the API is not already running, Playwright starts it with the local Ollama model so drafts are written by the AI.
--reportOpens the visual report afterwards. It has a screenshot of every step and a trace of any failure.
Running scenarios replaces the cases in your local queue with the four synthetic test cases. Nothing real is touched and nothing is filed. If the app is already running, it is reused; if not, it is started for you. Inside web/, npm run scenarios does the same as ./scenarios.sh.

Investigation stories

Open each preloaded case and follow it the way an investigator would. Run this group with ./scenarios.sh run stories --watch

1Suspicious transfer pattern → report consideration

ACC-4471 receives several deposits just under $10,000 and moves money on. The team scores it 100/100 and stops for a human.

  • Score 100/100 with a rule-by-rule breakdown
  • Money in $38,300 and out $28,000
  • Every finding names its specialist and source
  • Draft is marked as not filed
  • Workflow stops at the human checkpoint

./scenarios.sh run transfer-pattern --watch

2Routine transfer closes automatically

ACC-0001 is an ordinary $3,000 payment. The team scores it 15/100 and closes it without involving a human.

  • Score 15/100 → no escalation
  • Evidence critic is skipped
  • Case closes automatically with no human approval recorded

./scenarios.sh run routine-clear --watch

3Screening hit puts the case on hold

ACC-9999 involves a name on the illustrative screening list. The case is held until a human resolves it.

  • Recommendation is Hold
  • Screening method is labelled illustrative, not a live sanctions service
  • Suspicious names appear as plain text, never as hidden markers

./scenarios.sh run sanctions-hold --watch

4Borderline case goes to review

ACC-0040 has some signals but not enough for a report. The team recommends a human review.

  • Score 40/100 → review recommended
  • Needs your decision
  • Signals worth a closer look are listed

./scenarios.sh run needs-review --watch

The multi-agent team at work

See which specialists ran, in what order, and what the local AI wrote. Run this group with ./scenarios.sh run agents --watch

5Follow the specialist team step by step

Walk agent by agent through the transfer-pattern case and see what each specialist received and recorded.

  • The path matches the recorded run, in order
  • Next and Previous agent navigation work end to end
  • Timeline shows measured durations

./scenarios.sh run agent-team --watch

6One team, four decision paths

Compare the four recorded runs side by side, then jump into one of them.

  • All four outcomes come from real runs
  • "Open recorded run" lands on that case

./scenarios.sh run compare-paths --watch

7AI writes, code verifies

With the local model on, the AI writes each draft sentence and code checks it against verified facts. Without the model, the app says so honestly.

  • Every sentence shows the facts it cites
  • Sentences the verifier caught are shown, not hidden
  • Model, attempts and timing are visible
  • Without a model the draft is labelled stub narration

./scenarios.sh run ai-draft-verifier --watch best with local AI

8Ask for policy references without changing a case

Ask about a screening hold, inspect exact local notes and their background links, then try an unrelated question. LangChain retrieves, the local AI selects when available, and case decisions remain unchanged.

  • Case snapshot is separate from educational guidance
  • Every displayed passage has a local reference ID and source type
  • Unrelated questions abstain rather than inventing an answer
  • Risk score, recommendation and case activity remain unchanged

./scenarios.sh run policy-references --watch best with local AI

AI-designed stories

Invent your own story or let an AI red team try to beat the rules—code builds and checks everything. Run this group with ./scenarios.sh run studio --watch

9Invent a story and test the AI's prediction

Describe a situation in plain English. The local model designs a bounded recipe and predicts the outcome before the run; code builds the transactions and the same agent team decides.

  • The four-step pipeline is explained before anything runs
  • Code-built transactions use synthetic STORY- identifiers within bounds
  • The locked prediction is compared with the team's actual result

./scenarios.sh run story-studio --watch runs a new case

10Let an AI red team try to beat the rules

A red-team agent gets up to three rounds, learning which rules fired each time. The team investigates its best valid attempt and the result is scored honestly: caught, partly caught or slipped past.

  • Every round shows money moved, rule score and the rules that fired
  • Exactly one attempt is marked as investigated
  • The verdict matches the team's real recommendation, with blind spots explained

./scenarios.sh run red-team-challenge --watch runs a new case

11Story studio guardrails

Try a too-short story and one that hides an instruction. The studio refuses the first and neutralises the second before any model sees it.

  • Too-short stories cannot be submitted
  • Instruction-like text is flagged and redacted
  • The case is still an ordinary synthetic investigation

./scenarios.sh run studio-guardrails --watch runs a new case

Safety and honesty

Check what the tool refuses to do and how it behaves when things go wrong. Run this group with ./scenarios.sh run trust --watch

17Nothing is filed; decisions need a named human

Confirm the tool never files a report, only accepts a decision with a name, a reason and a checklist, and refuses customer data from the browser.

  • No control files a report; Submit stays disabled until the decision is complete
  • Code blocks actions the policy does not allow, and says why
  • The browser cannot send customer data, incomplete decisions or cross-site commands

./scenarios.sh run safety-limits --watch

18Record a decision with four-eyes escalation

A screening HOLD reaches you. Find the decision panel, see why closing is blocked, escalate it, then finish it as a different senior reviewer.

  • The banner says a decision is needed and Go to decision opens the panel
  • A HOLD cannot be closed at level 1; the reason is shown
  • The same person cannot finish their own escalation
  • The case closes with a named decision history

./scenarios.sh run human-decision --watch runs a new case

19When a case or the connection goes missing

Open a case that no longer exists, then lose the connection to the analysis service and get it back.

  • A missing case is explained
  • Lost connection shows Retry and marks data as stale
  • Retry recovers once the service is back

./scenarios.sh run connection-problems --watch
